summary.intent: The user wanted to understand the FireRedVAD example scripts, test them with their own audio file, and explore platform compatibility of the project dependencies.
summary.outcome: Successfully converted a user-recorded m4a file to WAV, ran VAD inference via a delegated agent (detecting 5 speech segments), and clarified that requirements.txt is CUDA-only while pyproject.toml optional deps support cross-platform installs.

repo: FireRedVAD uses Kaldi-style wav.scp manifests as an alternative to --wav_dir for specifying input files
The project venv uses Python 3.10 with torch installed; system Python (3.9.6) lacks torch and will fail with ModuleNotFoundError
inference_aed.sh defaults to --wav_dir mode; inference_vad.sh and inference_stream_vad.sh process all WAVs in wav/
VAD output: out/vad.txt (JSON lines), out/vad/ (trimmed WAV segments), and .TextGrid files written alongside source WAVs
requirements.txt pins torch==2.1.0+cu118 (CUDA 11.8 only); pyproject.toml [cpu]/[gpu] extras are platform-agnostic
workflow: afconvert is the native macOS CLI for m4a-to-WAV conversion: afconvert input.m4a output.wav -d LEI16 -f WAVE
say command can generate test WAV files directly: say -o test.wav --data-format=LEI16@16000 'text'
Orchestrator pattern: delegate implementation/inference tasks to subagents to stay free for parallel work
Always activate the project venv before running inference scripts to avoid missing torch imports

friction: VAD inference initially failed with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch' because the script invoked system Python 3.9.6 instead of the .venv Python 3.10.20 — agent had to explicitly use venv Python
QuickTime Player saves as .m4a not .wav, requiring an extra afconvert step before files can be used with FireRedVAD
requirements.txt is not usable on macOS at all due to CUDA-only torch wheel pinning
